headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can egress over allowlisted network paths while mem0 has no egress, creating limited leakage and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or parser bridge is documented. mem0 has no listed I/O surfaces and superset only exposes the Superset API, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy/paste or an external shared workspace, which is lower blast radius than default bridging.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies mem0 output into Superset inputs without review, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste handoff between agents.
Require human review of any text transferred from mem0 to Superset.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Add provenance labels to transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for any shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 shows no network egress, while superset has allowlisted egress and an API surface. With no touched data classes listed for either agent, there is no documented sensitive-data flow by default; leakage becomes plausible only if shared data is introduced into Superset workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in mem0 and then exported into Superset dashboards, those contents can leave the local boundary.
IF Superset is configured to query external services with user-provided text, that text may be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or regulated data in shared dashboards.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources.
Review outbound destinations in Superset allowlists.
Separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class tagging and egress policy checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can interact with mutable external surfaces in different ways: mem0 is a knowledge-management system and Superset exposes an API with allowlisted egress. Even without explicit write permissions, overlapping operational control over shared data products can create conflicts in default multi-agent workflows; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same downstream dataset or dashboard, concurrent updates can overwrite each other.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents through the same API token or workspace, mutable-state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces.
Use distinct API credentials.
Schedule non-overlapping update windows.
Add manual approval before writes.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 can supply remembered context and Superset can consume API-driven workflows, so A's output may become B's input without a documented verification step. That creates a plausible cascade where incorrect memory or summaries are rendered into analytics outputs; the pair lacks evidence of built-in cross-checking.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or automations ingest mem0-generated summaries, errors can propagate downstream.
IF no validation step is inserted between memory retrieval and analytics publication, false statements can be rendered as authoritative.
mitigations: Require source citations for transferred facts.
Add a human review step before publication.
Compare mem0 outputs against original records.
Limit mem0 to retrieval, not synthesis, for shared workflows.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch. mem0 has no touched data classes listed and Superset likewise lists none, so a residency or PHI pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either agent, compliance review must be redone.
IF deployment policies assign different retention or residency rules, a mismatch could emerge.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Map retention rules for each workspace.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
Review vendor residency terms.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
